Article Title: ‘Punched in the eyes, pushed into bus’: Journalists detained for second day at CJP protest despite IDs
Article Text:
Journalists covering protests in New Delhi faced detainment by police during their reporting duties





NEW DELHI: On a day SC said lawyers, journalists and other professionals should not be impeded from carrying out their professional duties, several journalists covering the protests were detained for a second day running Sunday.Among those detained were those working for established media organisations as well as independent online portals.A photojournalist, who wo­rks for a news agency, told TOI: “I was covering the AISA protest at RK Ashram when police started dispersing everyone in the area. When only mediapersons remained, they started to drag us by our necks into police vans even after we displayed our IDs, our cameras and shouted that we were from the press.The van had 7-8 journalists when they shut the doors and started moving. After a few kilometres, the van had to stop as police were removing barricades to make way. That was when I and two other journalists jumped out.”Nitin Katiyar, a digital journalist with Nayab World, was detained from the Connaught Place roundabout while covering the students’ march. Showing cuts below his right eye, Katiyar said that police detained him despite his showing “valid media credentials”.He alleged he was pushed inside the bus, where police allegedly punched him in the eyes when he protested.Among those detained were three Indian Express Hindi journalists. The organisation said in a post on X: “Three journalists from Indian Express Hindi — Shashwat, Siya, and Vijay — have been detained by Delhi Police while reporting. Even after informing the police that they were journalists who had come to do their job, they were forcibly put into a bus. The police bus was passing through Connaught Place in Delhi when Shashwat sent us a video he recorded on his mobile camera. Our colleague Siya’s phone has been seized by the police.”The three were later let go at Chhatrasal Stadium, the media organisation said.Pragya Mishra, an Uttar Pradesh-based journalist with Bharat Samachar, was also detained while she was covering the protests Saturday. On X, she posted a video of 5-6 policewomen grabbing her arms and legs while detaining her.“Take people into custody. Make them sit in police stations. Stop those who are showing the truth. Don’t let the pictures of the rape of democracy go out. Delhi Police is working on this agenda. I have a mic, the mic ID is there. I have everything, but in an extremely humiliating manner, Delhi Police deliberately threw me inside the bus and detained me. This is the capital of the country...” she posted on X. A journalist working with The Hindu was also detained in the evening. Several YouTubers and content creators were detained throughout the day from different protest spots, including RK Ashram, Connaught Place and near Jantar Mantar.There was no response from police over the issue till the time of going to press.
Article Summary: Among those detained were those working for established media organisations as well as independent online portals. Several YouTubers and content creators were detained throughout the day from different protest spots, including RK Ashram, Connaught Place and near Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: 'Attacked with stones, sticks': Clash between two groups during Navratri celebrations in Nalasopara; 10 injured
Article Text:
The injured were taken to Tulinj Hospital run by the Vasai Virar Municipal Corporation for treatment.





NALASOPARA: Navratri celebrations at Achole Mitra Mandal in Nalasopara East were marred by a violent clash between two groups on Sunday night, with both sides allegedly hurling stones and attacking each other with sticks and bamboo rods.Around 10 people were injured in the incident, triggering tension in the area.The clash took place at Achole when a two-wheeler rider had an argument with a tempo driver over a narrow road while the mandal's Navratri celebrations were underway.Mandal members allegedly assaulted the rider and drove him away. The rider later returned with his supporters, who allegedly attacked the mandal members with stones, sticks and bamboo rods.The injured were taken to Tulinj Hospital run by the Vasai Virar Municipal Corporation for treatment. Tulinj police registered a case against the attackers late on Sunday night.Vishal Singh, one of the injured mandal members, alleged that the rider, identified as Krishna, had been involved in a dispute and was driven away by mandal members.“He returned with 10 to 15 people carrying sticks and bamboo rods. They pelted stones at us and even damaged the mandal's idol,” Singh alleged.A woman injured in the clash claimed that around 50 to 60 people had arrived at the spot and assaulted her while she was standing there.However, Shiv Yadav, who claimed to be a friend of Krishna, gave a different account of the incident. He alleged that the mandal had not left enough space for people to pass through the road.“My friend Krishna, who was riding a two-wheeler, had an argument with the tempo driver because the road was narrow. Mandal members assaulted him, so we went to question them,” Yadav said.
Article Summary: Navratri celebrations at Achole Mitra Mandal in Nalasopara East marred by violent clash. Around 10 people were injured in the incident, triggering tension in the area. Tulinj police registered a case against the attackers late on Sunday night.

Article Title: Days before her wedding, engineering student found dead in Maharashtra gorge, boyfriend held
Article Text:
Naikwadi waterfall of Bhudargad





KOLHAPUR: A 25-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murdering his 23-year-old girlfriend, an engineering student whose body was found nearly 1,000ft below a cliff at Naikwadi waterfalls Maharashtra's Kolhapur.Police came to know of the death Saturday when Sripad Vadar walked into a PS and reported that Tarrannum Naik, a third-year student who lived with her maternal grandmother in Gargoti, had fallen into a gorge from a cliff.Police sent a team to the remote site and retrieved her body."He told us they had been in a relationship for five-and-a-half years and were distressed because her family had fixed her marriage elsewhere. According to him, the couple had decided to die by suicide together. He claimed she jumped into the gorge, but he lost his nerve at the last moment," sub-divisional police officer Vivek Patil said.Naikwadi waterfalls are deep inside forested terrain, about 50km from Gargoti. The falls were dry after the monsoon, and no visitors were in the area when the couple reached the spot Friday, police said.Police registered a case under section 140(3) of BNS, relating to wrongful confinement.But examination of messages exchanged between the couple raised doubts about Sripad's account."The chat history does not support the account he gave us about a suicide pact. The messages suggested Sripad was upset over Tarrannum's family's decision to get her married to someone else. That raised serious doubts and led us to invoke BNS section 103(1) for murder," Patil said.Accused Sripad, also from Gargoti, worked with his brother, a local contractor. On Sunday, a court remanded Sripad in police custody for five days.Police have seized mobile phones of both Tarrannum and the accused for forensic analysis. Police are awaiting the autopsy report.Tarrannum's last rites were performed at her native Patgaon. Her marriage had been fixed for Nov 12. Her death sparked protests in Gargoti, where residents marched to police station Sunday and demanded a fast-track trial.
Article Summary: Tarrannum Naik, 23, was found dead at Naikwadi waterfalls in Kolhapur, Maharashtra. Her boyfriend Sripad Vadar, 25, has been arrested on suspicion of murder. He told police the couple had decided to die by suicide together. Her death sparked protests in Gargoti, where residents marched to police station.

Article Title: Bhagat Singh’s photo appears against voter’s name in Ludhiana draft roll; error corrected, says official
Article Text:
An error was discovered on the electoral roll for Ludhiana East regarding a voter's name

By: Gurvinder.Singh





LUDHIANA: A draft electoral roll for Ludhiana East featured a photograph of revolutionary freedom fighter Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh against an ordinary voter's name, sparking sharp criticism over the accuracy and verification of local election machinery.The error appeared beside the entry for voter Aman Kumar in Gagandeep Colony within the draft roll published on Aug 13, 2026. Former Ludhiana East MLA and District Congress Committee (Urban) president Sanjay Talwar uncovered the discrepancy and challenged the integrity of multi-tiered oversight involving booth-level officers, supervisors, electoral registration officers, and the district election officer."If a photo of a member from the same family had been pasted against a voter's name, it might have been understandable," Talwar said. "But how can the photograph of Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh appear on the draft electoral roll and go unnoticed and get published?"Talwar linked the lapse to wider concerns raised by Rahul Gandhi of the Congress regarding voter list irregularities, questioning how many undetected errors remained in the system.District authorities issued a clarification stating that the incorrect image was inherited from a previous electoral roll and was carried over into the Aug draft. Officials confirmed the record has since been amended and that the corrected final roll will be published on Oct 12.Talwar countered that officials acted only after he exposed the issue publicly. "When we raised an objection, statements started coming that the error had been corrected in the final electoral roll," he said. Deputy commissioner Himanshu Jain, as district election officer, confirmed the resolution following a review with the relevant electoral registration officer. "The mistake was pushed from the previous electoral roll. However, it has been corrected in the final electoral roll," Jain said.In a post on X, Ludhiana MP and former Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring too flagged the discrepancy.
Article Summary: A draft electoral roll for Ludhiana East featured a photograph of revolutionary freedom fighter Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh against an ordinary voter's name. The error appeared beside the entry for voter Aman Kumar in Gagandeep Colony within the draft roll published on Aug 13, 2026. Officials confirmed the record has since been amended and that the corrected final roll will be published on Oct 12.

Article Title: Bill Gates to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who says AI fears sound like "bad science fiction": All responsible AI leaders, including you, are telling the world...
Article Text:
Bill Gates says AI is more dangerous than cars, planes or medicines, and needs a regulatory middle ground

Bill Gates says a middle ground on AI regulation exists

Sam Altman's UN speech warned against both AI extremes

Bill Gates's AI essay sets out the safeguards he wants

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has pushed back on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 's warning against AI "doomerism", saying every responsible AI leader, Altman included, is already telling the world that artificial intelligence is "very concerning". Altman had recently said some of the scenarios people imagine about AI are "so dystopian that they sound like the plot of bad science fiction movies. "In a Sunday interview with Jake Tapper, Gates, who has described AI as more dangerous than nuclear weapons, agreed that the risk can get overblown when people "act like all of humanity is at risk". But he said AI is more dangerous than cars, planes or medicines, all of which are heavily regulated, and that "there are some grim possibilities if we don't maintain control."Gates said the AI industry is doing its job by raising the alarm. What isn't getting across, he argued, is that the risks can be kept down "if we're judicious". He blamed part of that on governments that swing between two extremes: "let's not have any safeguards" or "let's completely stop this".The world found a workable balance for planes, cars and drugs, he said, and AI needs the same. Finding that balance is something "we don't have a lot of sophistication" in right now, he added, "but I do believe that middle ground exists."He repeated the point in a post on X, writing that safeguards won't eliminate every harm but can help stop misuse by bad actors.Altman's "bad science fiction" line came from his address to the UN Security Council on September 23. In the same speech, he said OpenAI wants to avoid both blind optimism and doomerism, and walk a middle path. He also flagged two ways AI could go badly: humans losing control of it, or too much power ending up in too few hands.That speech had a line Gates could easily have written. Altman told the Council that a risk of catastrophe, whether 10% or 0.1%, is not "remotely acceptable". Since then, he has struck a looser tone, saying on a podcast that "the world should accept some bad things happening", such as hacks and scams, because people will do far more good with AI.Gates's stance traces back to a nearly 6,000-word essay he published in August. In it, he named three big risks: jobs disappearing for good, bad actors using AI for cyberattacks and bioterrorism, and AI companions affecting how children grow up.His fixes include a new national and international framework to manage the AI transition, a "Human Reserved" set of jobs such as caregiving that stay with people, and a tax on AI tokens and robots to fund retraining and a stronger safety net. In an interview around the essay, he was blunter about the industry's own plans: "Self-regulation on the most dangerous tool ever invented? No, thanks!"Gates also named Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei alongside Altman. Amodei published an essay in September arguing that AI's frontier should be paced more slowly, with outside evaluators placed inside AI companies to check their safety work.So the three men agree on more than the "doomerism" label suggests. Where they split is on how much regulation the industry should accept, and how soon. Gates, now 70 and no longer running a company, has said he plans to raise the issue with lawmakers every time he visits Washington.
Article Summary: Gates says AI is more dangerous than cars, planes or medicines, and needs a regulatory middle ground. He blamed part of that on governments that swing between two extremes: "Let's not have any safeguards" or "let's completely stop this" Gates's stance traces back to an essay he published in August.

Article Title: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar joined US Army as lieutenant colonel in 2025; his job: find coders that Army doesn’t know it has and turn them into...
Article Text:
Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar is helping the US Army find coders hiding in its ranks

Why the US Army struggles to use its tech talent

What is Detachment 201 , the Army’s tech executive corps

Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar has a second job in the US Army Reserve, and it has little to do with weapons or battlefield software. Speaking to CBS News on Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan, Sankar said his main role as a lieutenant colonel is helping the Army find soldiers who can code, and then making sure that talent is put to proper use.Sankar works with the Army’s G-1, the department that handles personnel and human resources. The problem he described is structural. The Army has skilled programmers in its ranks, but its career system was built for an industrial-era military, a model Sankar likened to Napoleonic codes. A soldier at the E-4 grade, a junior enlisted rank, could be an exceptional coder and still have no clear path to doing that work in uniform.Sankar told CBS News that “the Army is drowning in talent,” referring to uniformed soldiers who know how to write code. The catch is that their skills don’t follow rank. The Army assigns roles by seniority, but coding ability doesn’t come with stripes.His work focuses on three questions. How does the Army spot these soldiers, how does it stop them from getting lost in the system, and how does it place them on projects that use what they can do? The goal is to turn them into assets the military draws on instead of leaving them in roles unrelated to their skills.Sankar was sworn in in June 2025 as part of Detachment 201, the Army’s Executive Innovation Corps. The name nods to HTTP status code 201, which signals that a new resource has been created on a server. The first cohort included Meta’s Andrew Bosworth and two executives with OpenAI roots, Kevin Weil and Bob McGrew. Army officials have credited Sankar with pitching the idea and recruiting the other three.The executives serve around 120 hours a year and hold the rank of lieutenant colonel because of their private-sector expertise. They were spared basic training but still face fitness tests and marksmanship training.The arrangement has raised questions about conflicts of interest. Brennan pointed out that Palantir holds billions of dollars in US government contracts. Sankar said the Defense Department’s lawyers manage this closely, and that reservists can only work on projects where they have no conflict.He also spoke about why he signed up. Sankar’s family fled violence in Lagos when he was a child, and he called serving in the US military the greatest honour. He said his late father would have loved to see him attend a service academy. Now 44, he said he hopes he has more to give the country today than he did at 24.
Article Summary: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar is helping the US Army find coders hiding in its ranks. He is part of Detachment 201, the Army’s Executive Innovation Corps. The goal is to turn them into assets the military draws on instead of leaving them in roles unrelated to their skills.

Article Title: ‘Preparation is important’: Abhishek Sharma explains how he stays ahead of opposition bowlers
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

INDORE: Abhishek Sharma likes to do "uncomfortable" things during practice sessions. He believes that such preparation keeps him battle-ready and ensures he is not caught by "surprise" when facing world-class bowlers.With Roston Chase having dismissed the left-hander twice earlier in the series, and Abhishek's weakness against off-spinners well documented, West Indies began with the 34-year-old offie in an attempt to counter him from the word go.The 26-year-old knew what the visitors were trying to exploit, but this time he was ready. He bided his time, played out the first over he faced from Chase and, once settled, launched into him in the next. A 111.6 kmph faster one was smashed through the covers for four while a much slower delivery was deposited over wide long-off for six, and the dose was repeated as he struck another six over covers.Abhishek never looked back thereafter as he raced to his 14th T20I fifty and finished with a 30-ball 69. During his innings at the Holkar Stadium on Sunday, he achieved another staggering feat, scoring 72 per cent of his runs through the off-side.In the process, he became the fastest batter to score 2,000 T20I runs. He reached the landmark in just 1,024 balls, 140 fewer than the previous record holder, Suryakumar Yadav , who took 1,164 deliveries to get there.Abhishek's career strike rate stands at 195.95, and he feels the preparation he puts in behind the scenes is crucial to sustaining that approach."I think preparation is important. If I want to just continue playing like this, and that's the plan for the team, then preparation really matters. I always believe in that. It always depends on the teams and the bowlers I'm going to face. So, whenever I have time, it's (preparation) very specific... how bowlers are going to plan against me, how I'm going to execute my plan and dominate," said Abhishek."As a batter, if you have to face world-class bowlers, you have to be ready for all the plans. I always want that preparation in practice which makes me a bit uncomfortable so that I wouldn't be surprised in the match. So I always allow myself to be in that position during training," he added.West Indies allrounder Shamar Springer also lauded Abhishek's innings, which circumvented their plans and forced them to switch to a 'Plan B' that involved bowling a defensive line to him."He is a world-class player. But I guess our 'Plan B' was to just be as defensive as possible and try to make him get singles and twos. It was just a matter of trying to pull him back because there's not much control you can really have here. The wickets are so good and those players are world-class players and they're the best for a reason. So, it's not really much you can do besides be defensive," said Springer.Earlier in the year, during the T20 World Cup, Abhishek struggled against off-spinners and almost every team targeted that weakness. During that period, he would often try to force his way out of trouble.Eight months later, while Abhishek's ability to destroy attacks at the top remains intact, his willingness to wait just a little longer before launching into the opposition has made this version of him an even scarier proposition for opponents to dismantle.
Article Summary: India's Abhishek Sharma became the fastest batter to score 2,000 T20I runs. He reached the landmark in just 1,024 balls, 140 fewer than the previous record holder, Suryakumar Yadav. He scored 72 per cent of his runs through the off-side during his innings at the Holkar Stadium.

Article Title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery: What we know about his health and upcoming plans
Article Text:
Pope Leo XIV is scheduled for surgery to extract a lung nodule and is anticipated to recover within a week.

What is a lung nodule? Can it be cancerous?

Surgery planned, followed by a week of recovery

Does the pope retain authority while unconscious?

Cardinal Tagle appointed dean ahead of surgery

Pope Leo XIV is preparing to undergo surgery to remove a localised nodule in his lung, which was detected at a very early stage. The procedure is the first reported medical event of his 17-month papacy.The 71-year-old pontiff is otherwise considered healthy and physically fit. Here is a look at what is known about the lung nodule, his planned treatment, the possible impact on his engagements and the question of papal authority during a medical emergency.A lung nodule is a small abnormal spot in the lung measuring less than 3 centimetres (approximately 1.2 inches) in diameter. According to the american cancer society, such nodules are sometimes discovered during CT scans carried out to investigate other conditions, including injuries or lung infections.Lung nodules may be benign or malignant, making timely medical assessment important to establish their nature.Dr Stephen Liu, a lung cancer specialist at Georgetown's Lombardi comprehensive cancer center, said the prognosis is “excellent” when a cancerous nodule is detected and removed at an early stage. In some cases, surgery alone may be enough to treat the condition.Leo said the nodule was identified during “recent medical tests”.The Vatican said on Monday that the check-up was “routine” and had not been prompted by any specific health concern.The Vatican announced that Leo would undergo the procedure during the first days of the week. He is expected to remain in hospital for around a week to recover.The pope will receive treatment at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, officially known as the Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic. The private, non-profit catholic teaching hospital has a dedicated apartment for pontiffs on its 10th floor, which includes a private chapel.Leo's predecessor, Pope Francis, was treated at the same hospital before his death in May 2025 following a prolonged illness that included a respiratory crisis.St John Paul II also spent considerable time at Gemelli and famously referred to it as “Vatican III”, alongside the Vatican itself and the papal summer residence at Castel Gandolfo.Will the procedure affect Leo's schedule and foreign trip?The pope has several engagements lined up for the week, including his regular meetings and a public mass scheduled for Wednesday. The mass is due to mark the end of a weeklong conference on family ministry, but Vatican officials indicated on Sunday that Leo might not attend.His planned overseas visit from November 6 to 17 to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru could also be affected by the operation and recovery period.The itinerary involves 12 flights, two helicopter journeys and considerable changes in altitude during the Peru leg. It remains uncertain whether the medical procedure will require any changes to the schedule.According to the Leo, he is still intended to undertake the trip, stated during the Sunday.The Vatican has no specific rules determining, who assumes a pope's powers if he becomes completely incapacitated. As a result, Leo would remain pope and retain his authority even while unconscious during surgery.Previous pontiffs continued to exercise their responsibilities during extended hospital stays. Pope Francis and St John Paul II made appointments and issued laws and statements while undergoing treatment.The Vatican's day-to-day affairs are already managed by a team of officials, but the absence of a formal framework for a pope, who becomes unable to govern has attracted increasing attention.Advances in medical treatment and longer life expectancies have intensified calls for the church to establish clearer arrangements for a pontiff who becomes seriously ill or incapacitated for an extended period.Two days before announcing his planned operation, Leo approved an important appointment within the church's leadership.On Friday, he named Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, 69, as the new dean of the College of Cardinals. Tagle succeeds Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re, 92, whose term had been extended by Pope Francis in the weeks leading up to his death.The dean plays a key role during the transition between popes. The position involves presiding over the previous pontiff's funeral and helping lead closed-door meetings of cardinals ahead of the conclave, where they discuss the church's priorities and future direction.If the dean is younger than 80, when the conclave begins, he also presides over the secret election of the next pope in the Sistine Chapel.
Article Summary: Pope Leo XIV is scheduled for surgery to extract a lung nodule. The procedure is the first reported medical event of his 17-month papacy. The 71-year-old pontiff is otherwise considered healthy and physically fit. He is expected to remain in hospital for around a week to recover. The Vatican has no rules determining, who assumes a pope's powers if he becomes completely incapacitated.

Article Title: Weekend farmers find their patch of peace in NCR
Article Text:
For a growing number of working professionals, farming offers more than a hobby — it is a way to slow down, switch off and reconnect with nature

People are looking for a relationship with nature

Farming is not everyone’s cup of tea

Kapil says urban farming appeals to corporate professionals seeking relief from work stress

People are looking for a relationship with nature

Farm clubs allow professionals to purchase a patch of land and, with assistance from traditional farmers, nurture and grow their produce

Focus on

organic produce

, inclusivity

If you look only at the economics, farming in Gurgaon may not make sense. But if you include health, joy, community, nature and quality of life, the equation changes completely. Manas Arvind, co-founder of Gurgaon Organic Farmers Market

'It required a shift in mindset, from a routine job to a new world without an immediate, regular source of income'

'Wanted to step back from corporate'





Community experiences are all the rage, from art workshops and jam sessions to nature walks and terrarium-making. As working professionals look for ways to disconnect from the corporate hustle, farm clubs in Gurgaon run by ex-professionals are offering them a chance to get their hands dirty, grow their own produce and reconnect with nature. Gurgaon’s remaining farmland is becoming an escape of sorts for those looking to trade the office for the khet, if only for a weekend.While starting a farm from scratch may not be for everyone, farm clubs allow professionals to purchase a patch of land and with assistance from traditional farmers, nurture and grow their produce.Noting the specific appeal to urban farming, Mukesh Rana, co-founder of Gurgaon Farm Club who left his corporate job two years ago, says, “After the pandemic, we have seen the appeal grow. Everybody wants to do it because farming looks very lucrative, but there are a lot of challenges. We take care of those challenges while allowing people to fulfil their dream of farming. If someone rents a small piece of land and manages it themselves, it can cost at least ₹50,000 a month to maintain. Our model allows them to enjoy the experience without having to take on all those responsibilities themselves.”Kapil Mandawewala was working in finance in the US before he came back to India and started Edible Routes in 2014.“I had already been farming for about six years before I started this. And this was just an extension of it. That was pure farming I was doing. But then gradually, I shifted into urban farming because I was enjoying this process more,” he says. Talking about the shift, he adds, “It's been very fulfilling, but a very slow process at the same time. Because in nature you have to go with the yearly seasonal cycles. Things take time to grow and build. I've enjoyed it, but it takes a lot of time.” He adds that due to the time-consuming and expensive nature of the process, many people give up early on, or hesitate to begin their journey.Manas Arvind, co-founder of Gurgaon Organic Farmers Market who has been organising the weekly market for five years shares how urban farming is changing Gurgaon’s landscape. “Gurgaon was essentially a city that grew over agricultural land as an extension of the National Capital Region. A large part of the original agricultural land was eventually acquired or sold for development. Many of the intergenerational farming families moved away from farming as land values increased. At the same time, people who came to Gurgaon for corporate jobs, businesses and professional opportunities began looking for a different relationship with land and nature.”Kapil notes why urban farming is an option for corporate professionals, “It’s probably the burnout of working in the corporate world, the stress. And gaining a better connection to food and nature. Humans are naturally inclined towards that. It's just a matter of being open to it.”Mukesh shares, “We have a members’ community where we share knowledge about farming practices, especially during the sowing season. It’s a community where we share knowledge and work together. Once a month, we also organise a high tea for members, where they can meet, make new friends and spend time together. So it’s a combination of social and technical aspects — we grow natural food, meet regularly, spend time at the farm, connect with nature and learn about farming. ”Talking about the growth of the ecosystem, Manas says, “I’m very positive about urban farming. But I don’t think the future should be about creating an exclusive club of affluent urban people who can afford to farm. Inclusivity is the key challenge. We need to bring traditional farmers, small farmers, urban farmers, consumers, young people and food entrepreneurs into the same ecosystem.” While Kapil adds, “Getting organic produce is a part of the aspiration. But I won't say urban farming is growing. It's quite stable. There is a very small group of people who enjoy this activity. I would not say it's grown significantly but there is a study stream of people who want to get into this.”Mekhla Maheshwari, founder of Zemya Farms in Gurgaon shares, “I started Zemya as I wanted to step back from corporate and follow a bit of my passion of connecting back to the earth and soil, making our urban lives more meaningful and connected to natural surroundings and living. That's what made me passionate about building a place that brings more urban people to experience the joy of growing their food and connect back to the earth and soil in the times that we live in. The disconnect with food in people in urban cities is real and that's what people are looking for. A place that they can trust, which is affordable and also addresses getting back the connection to the natural environment and food."Talking about the shift from corporate, she says, "Initially, it was full of excitement in the beginning, but the practical aspects started hitting too. Finding the right farmer teams, managing the expectations of farm members with seasonal cycles and operational challenges — there were many challenges, but it has also been a very fulfilling and meaningful experience, full of new learnings. It required a shift in mindset, from a routine job to a new world without an immediate, regular source of income. "
Article Summary: For a growing number of working professionals, farming offers more than a hobby. Farm clubs in Gurgaon run by ex-professionals are offering them a chance to get their hands dirty, grow their own produce and reconnect with nature. Manas Arvind, co-founder of Gurga on Organic Farmers Market, says urban farming is changing the city's landscape.

Article Title: Juryspeak: Times50Finest: 'Fine dining is about fineness of thought': Ranveer Brar
Article Text:
‘The best restaurants are ultimately the ones that are difficult to replace’

‘There’s tremendous pride in regional cuisines’

‘The word fine is about fineness of thought’

‘Go deeper before you go wider’





From Lucknow’s kitchens to global culinary stages, Chef Ranveer Brar has made food a vehicle for memory, culture and storytelling. In a conversation around Times 50 Finest Restaurants of India, the jury member reflects on culinary maturity, the growing confidence in regional Indian cuisine and why the country’s restaurants must contribute to the world’s understanding of food. Excerpts:For me, a great restaurant today is about clarity of intent. It doesn’t necessarily have to be expensive, luxurious or technically complicated. It needs to know why it exists, what it wants to say and, most importantly, how it wants you to feel when you leave. For me, the best restaurants are ultimately the ones that are difficult to replace. You leave and think: I couldn’t have had that experience anywhere else.The biggest change I’ve seen is confidence. There was a time when sophistication in Indian restaurants often meant borrowing a vocabulary from somewhere else, whether it was technique, plating, ingredients or even the way we spoke about our food. That’s changing. Today there’s tremendous pride in regional cuisines, indigenous ingredients, forgotten techniques, provenance and our own ways of eating.That fine dining has to look fine dining. Expensive ingredients, elaborate plating, tweezers, tiny portions, a lot happening on the plate. None of those things automatically make food sophisticated. For me, the word fine is about fineness of thought. How deeply have you understood the ingredient? Why is something on that plate? What have you chosen to leave out?Sometimes we’re in such a hurry to take Indian food to the world that we start translating it for the world. We simplify it, decorate it or try to make it fit somebody else’s idea of sophistication. I think young chefs should do exactly the opposite. Travel within India. Talk to grandmothers, farmers, halwais, home cooks and craftspeople. Understand ingredients, dialects, seasons, techniques and the reasons behind traditions. Don’t worry so much about making Indian food global. Understand Indian food so deeply that the world becomes curious enough to come to you.The Times 50 Finest Restaurants of India will be revealed at an event in Mumbai tomorrow.
Article Summary: The Times 50 Finest Restaurants of India will be revealed at an event in Mumbai tomorrow. The jury member reflects on culinary maturity, the growing confidence in regional Indian cuisine and why restaurants must contribute to the world’s understanding of food. ‘The best restaurants are ultimately the ones that are difficult to replace’

Article Title: ​In drought-hit Marathwada, Soybean yield crashes by over 73% to 410 kg per hectare
Article Text:
Wilted soybean crops from Nanded district

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Soybean farmers from Marathwada have suffered severe yield loss this kharif season, with initial crop cutting experiment data showing a steep drop in per-hectare production.As per the early official figures for Beed district, one of the top individual districts with large soybean acreage, the average soybean yield over the last five years was 1,534.2 kg per hectare. In the current season, the yield has plummeted to just 410 kg per hectare — a drop of around 1,124 kg or over 73%.A sharp fall has highlighted extensive crop damage this season and raised concerns about financial stress among soybean growers, who account for a major proportion of drought-hit farmers in Marathwada. The region recorded sowing across more than 46 lakh hectares last kharif season, including over 25 lakh hectares under soybean.A senior official from the agriculture department, said soybean is most vulnerable to vagaries of monsoon even if it is a popular crop. “The crop requires timely sowing between June 15 and July 15 and good early-season soil moisture, followed by regular spells of rain. The delayed arrival of monsoon this year together with extended dry spells in Aug and Sept took a toll on the crop from rain-fed cultivation,” he said.Authorities said the issue of upto 40% chances of yield reductions under delayed monsoon further compounded due to absence of rains in crucial stages of growth of soybean crops, leading to massive crash in yields. Anwar Shaikh, a soybean farmer from Mukhed taluka of Nanded district , said he has already sold his pair of bulls owned by him to pay his debts by the end of September.“I have completely lost my soyabean crop. Moreover, our talukas are excluded from the first list of talukas where drought-relief measures will be undertaken. Despair is gripping me like never before,” he said.Central drought assessment team chief and Union agriculture ministry joint secretary Muktanand Agrawal on Saturday directed Beed district administrations to complete pending crop-cutting experiments on time and accurately record losses, enabling drought-affected farmers to receive crop-damage compensation before Diwali. During his visit, Agrawal stressed field verification alongside technical data to determine drought severity.
Article Summary: Soybean farmers from Marathwada have suffered severe yield loss this kharif season. Initial crop cutting experiment data shows a steep drop in per-hectare production. A sharp fall has highlighted extensive crop damage this season. It has raised concerns about financial stress among soybean growers.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke’s mother: ‘Why is govt detaining him when it is not arresting rapists?’
Article Text:
For the Dipke family, Saturday became a day marked by both political confrontation and personal loss.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Barely hours after CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained by Delhi police upon landing in the national capital on Saturday morning, his grandmother died at the family home in Maharashtra’s Hingoli district. The Dipke family is not sure if he will be allowed to attend her last rites on Sunday.The double blow triggered an emotional response from Dipke’s family members, who accused govt of targeting him and demanded answers over his detention.“My mother, Savitribai, breathed her last around 12.30pm at our home in Santuk Pimpri village. She was unwell and bedridden for some time. Abhijeet and she shared a close bond,” said Bhagwanrao Dipke, the CJP founder’s father.“Since his illegal detention, we have not been able to speak to him and we don’t know his whereabouts. We don’t know whether he will be returning to attend his grandmother’s last rites on Sunday morning,” he added. As he travelled to Hingoli to attend his mother’s funeral, Bhagwanrao questioned the police action. He demanded that Delhi Police disclose the legal grounds for detaining his son and asked what offence he had committed.Despite the detention, Bhagwanrao said the family would stand by his son. “I am not worried about Abhijeet. He has chosen to take up this cause, and we will stand by him.”Dipke’s mother, Anita, also lashed out at govt. “Why is govt detaining Abhijeet when it is not arresting rapists? They (police personnel) went into the aircraft to detain him. What kind of rule is this?” she asked.Recalling a conversation before one of his trips, she said she had warned her son that he could be detained at any time. “He told me, ‘Mummy, it is not like that. I want to do something for the country. I belong to this country’,” she said. Dipke had declared before reaching Delhi that he was prepared to face arrest.For the Dipke family, Saturday became a day marked by both political confrontation and personal loss. Even as they prepare for her last rites, the uncertainty over if Abhijeet Dipke will be allowed to bid a final farewell to his grandmother now hangs over the family members.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained by Delhi police upon landing in the national capital on Saturday morning. Hours later, his grandmother died at the family home in Maharashtra’s Hingoli district. The Dipke family is not sure if he will be allowed to attend her last rites on Sunday.

Article Title: Wrestlers wield grass cutters to protest neglect of Kolhapur akhada
Article Text:
Wrestlers cleaned Shahu Khasbaug Maidan

Kolhapur

:





More than 100 wrestlers and wrestling enthusiasts gathered at the iconic Shahu Khasbaug Kusti Maidan early on Sunday, not for a bout but to cut the waist-high grass that has overrun the ground.The protest was aimed at highlighting the authorities’ apathy towards maintaining the historic wrestling arena, modelled on European arenas built over a century ago.Apart from tall grass and weeds, the protesters found empty liquor bottles, cigarette packets and butter papers used to wrap scented tobacco sold at pan shops.The podium at the maidan was gutted in a fire two years ago, along with the Keshavrao Bhosale Natyagruha. The cause of the fire and how it spread remain unclear.“The govt allocated Rs 25 crore to restore the theatre and rebuild the podium. Two years later, while the theatre has been rebuilt, the podium remains damaged,” said Ramesh More , convener of the District Citizens Forum.Wrestlers said the annual wrestling season had begun and the maidan was a key venue for practice sessions and major competitions. However, the overgrown ground was unfit for use.“The ground is not ready. Where will we practise? The sport will become extinct because of the authorities’ negligence,” said a protester.The protesters warned that they would stage demonstrations outside the residences of MP Shahu Chhatrapati and city MLA Rajesh Kshirsagar if the ground was not made ready within eight days.
Article Summary: More than 100 wrestlers and wrestling enthusiasts gathered at the iconic Shahu Khasbaug Kusti Maidan early on Sunday. The protest was aimed at highlighting the authorities’ apathy towards maintaining the historic arena. The podium at the maidan was gutted in a fire two years ago.

Article Title: Satara police arrest three in jewellery shop theft, recover Rs9.15 lakh stolen goods
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





The Satara city police have arrested three suspects, including a minor, for allegedly breaking open the shutter of a jewellery shop at Shete Chowk in Satara and stealing goods worth Rs9.15 lakh. The theft took place on the night of Oct 7.The three suspects, all from Satara, were apprehended following a police investigation into the incident after Akshay Ankush Shinde (31), a resident of Patkhal, filed a complaint with the city police station on Oct 8.The suspects were identified as Rehan Anwar Sheikh (20), a resident of Shaniwar Peth, and Shubham Suresh Hadge (19), a resident of Kesarkar Peth. The minor has also been taken into custody.S G Mhetre, police inspector, Satara City police, said, “The incident happened on Oct 7th at midnight. The suspected gang broke open the shutters of Avadhoot Jewellers shop. They stole gold rings worth Rs1.30 lakh, nose rings worth Rs1.25 lakh, silver bangles and anklets worth Rs1.53 lakh each, silver ornaments worth Rs55,000, small and large idols worth Rs33,000 and rings, zodiac stones, and tax money from the shop.The next day after the incident, the city police conducted a panchnama and immediately started an investigation.The jeweller’s shop had a CCTV camera. However, it came to light that the thieves also stole the entire set of machines, including the DVR and CCTV camera, during the robbery, which hampered the police’s preliminary investigation.“While the investigation was going on through technical and conventional information, some suspects were seen in the CCTV footage that was gathered from the area. The suspects were then arrested, who confessed to the theft,” added Mhetre.
Article Summary: The Satara city police have arrested three suspects, including a minor, for allegedly breaking open the shutter of a jewellery shop. The theft took place on the night of Oct 7. The suspects were identified as Rehan Anwar Sheikh (20), a resident of Shaniwar Peth, and Shubham Suresh Hadge (19) The minor has also been taken into custody.
